title: Client Accounts Assistant
description:
This upmarket global real estate agency with anenviable reputationand an international network of offices, currently has an opportunity for a Client Accounts Assistant to join the team in Richmond-upon-Thames.

Based within the vibrant lettings head office, you will be working closely with the tenancy progression, property management and client services teams. The accounts team whilst hardworking and proactive, is equally friendly and sociable. They have created an environment that's full of energy aiming for a good work/life balance.

As the client accounts assistant, you will be able to manage an ever-changing workload by good prioritisation, using your own initiative and be a methodical thinker. If this sounds like you, please get in touch!

Responsibilities will include:
- Answering and solve queries from landlords, tenants, the other head office departments and branches
- Processing terminations
- Processing payments of deposit returns to outgoing tenants, as well as ensuring all accounts are accurate for new tenants on the system
- Ensuring correct fees are collected from landlords
- Managing daily payments to landlords including rent and credits
- Importing renewal deals
- Spotting inconsistencies and recognising 'red flags' and take the appropriate actions
- Being a team player and assisting your team with additional administrative tasks as and when required.

Personal specification:
- Previous experience in relevant accounting role in a high-volume environment
- Experience handling accounts within estate agency would be preferred
- Accurate IT skills and methodical approach
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Good knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Outlook, Word and Excel to perform required tasks
- Ability to process and organise workload quickly but accurately
- Customer service experience.

The salary on offer for this client accounts assistant role will be in the region of £30,000 to £32,000 dependent on previous experience, plus an annual discretionary bonus. Benefits include 25 days holiday plus bank holidays, Christmas and New Year, pension, private health insurance after probation, life assurance, discount portal, and more.

Working hours are Monday to Friday from 9am to 5.30pm.

title: Accounts Administrator
company: Capital Outsourcing Group Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Accounts Administrator

Join a growing team and play a key role in keeping the finances running smoothly.

Salary: £30,000 per annum

Full-time Permanent Monday-Friday, 40 hrs

We're looking for a highly organised and detail-focused Accounts Administrator to join a busy finance team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who enjoys working with numbers, takes pride in getting things right and thrives in a role where accuracy, organisation and teamwork really matter.

You'll play an important part in supporting the day-to-day finance function, working across accounts payable, customer accounts, payments, reconciliations and general financial administration.

What you'll be doing

Your responsibilities will include:
- Processing purchase invoices and credit notes
- Reviewing supplier statements and ensuring invoices are received and processed accurately
- Supporting the management and collection of outstanding customer balances
- Setting up new customer and supplier accounts
- Processing employee expenses
- Preparing and making supplier payments
- Handling incoming finance-related queries by phone and email
- Processing payments securely over the phone
- Posting bank transactions using accounting software
- Managing the finance team inbox and ensuring queries are dealt with promptly
- Supporting the release of orders where payment requirements have been met
- Providing general finance administration and support to the wider team
- Taking on additional duties and projects as required

What we're looking for

We're looking for someone who is:
- Experienced in a Financial Administrator, Accounts Assistant or similar role
- Highly organised with excellent attention to detail
- Comfortable working with financial information and deadlines
- Confident using accounting systems and Microsoft Office
- Enjoys working in a fast paced and busy environment
- Reliable, proactive and able to manage competing priorities
- A positive team player who is happy to get stuck in

Previous experience using SAP or similar business/accounting systems would be advantageous, but isn't essential.

Why join us?

This is more than a processing role. You'll become an important part of a collaborative finance team and have the opportunity to develop your skills across a broad range of financial activities.

We offer:
- £30, 000 annual salary
- 25 days' holiday plus bank holidays
- Company pension
- On-site parking
- A supportive team environment
- Opportunities to develop your finance experience

The role

Salary: £30,000 per annum

Contract: Full-time, Permanent

Hours: Monday-Friday, 40 hrs

Working arrangement: Office-based

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Our client is seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Bookkeeper to manage the day-to-day financial records of the business.

The successful candidate will be responsible for maintaining accurate financial information, processing transactions, reconciling accounts, preparing management reports, supporting payroll, and ensuring compliance with relevant financial regulations.

This role requires excellent organisational skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to work independently while supporting the wider business.

Duties of Bookkeeper:
- Maintain accurate day-to-day financial records using the company's accounting software.
- Process and reconcile sales and purchase ledger transactions.
- Raise customer invoices and allocate customer receipts.
- Process supplier invoices, reconcile supplier statements, and prepare payment runs.
- Perform daily, weekly, and monthly bank reconciliations.
- Manage petty cash and company credit card transactions.
- Monitor cash flow and maintain accurate financial records.
- Carry out credit control activities, including chasing outstanding payments and resolving customer account queries.
- Prepare and submit VAT returns in line with HMRC requirements.
- Process journals, accruals, prepayments, and general ledger adjustments.
- Reconcile balance sheet accounts and investigate any discrepancies.
- Assist with payroll preparation, pension administration, and employee expense processing.
- Produce monthly management accounts and financial reports for management.
- Support budgeting and cash flow forecasting.
- Prepare year-end schedules and liaise with external accountants during the year-end accounts process.
- Maintain the fixed asset register where applicable.
- Ensure all financial records are accurate, complete, and compliant with company procedures and relevant legislation.
- Maintain confidential financial information and ensure data accuracy at all times.
- Assist with audits and provide supporting documentation as required.
- Maintain organised financial filing systems, both electronic and paper-based.
- Identify opportunities to improve financial processes and internal controls.
- Respond promptly to supplier, customer, and internal finance queries.
- Support the wider business with financial and administrative tasks as required.
- Ensure all month-end and year-end deadlines are met.
- Carry out any other bookkeeping, finance, or administrative duties appropriate to the role.

title: Credit Controller
description:
A Credit Controller in the retail industry will focus on managing the day-to-day credit control processes to ensure smooth cash flow and minimise outstanding debts. This role is key to supporting the Accounting & Finance department in maintaining accurate records and fostering good relationships with clients.

Client Details

An organisation in the retail industry, offering products and services to customers nationwide.

Description
- Monitor and manage debtor accounts to ensure timely payments.
- Prepare and issue invoices, statements and reminders to clients.
- Resolve payment discrepancies and address customer queries.
- Maintain accurate records of all credit control activities.
- Liaise with internal departments to ensure account accuracy and compliance.
- Prepare regular reports on outstanding debts and account statuses.
- Assist in implementing credit control policies and procedures.
- Support the Accounting & Finance team with ad-hoc administrative tasks.

Profile

A successful Credit Controller should have:
- Strong experience in credit control or a related accounting role.
- Familiarity with accounting systems and software.
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills.
- Good attention to detail and organisational abilities.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and customer service.
- Knowledge of credit control processes.

Job Offer
- Salary ranging from £35,000 to £38,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Permanent position within the retail industry.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

If you require any adjustments or accommodations during the recruitment process, we'll work with you to ensure you can perform at your best.

description:
